current_round.prompt:
From: Buddy Williams <buddy.williams@insurity.com>
Subject: After latest release of Refine, goals are failing.

Body:
After update goals are failing.  I check with Claude and this is what it found.

Refine rejected your completion signal: does not match the required schema:
  guidance_applied[0]: invalid type: string "guidance-1", expected usize.

  Here's what's happening:

  1. Agent completes its work (dotnet build ✅,  0 StyleCop warnings ✅,  dotnet test ✅  all passing)
  2. Agent writes its completion signal with guidance_applied: ["guidance-1", "guidance-2", ...] (string IDs)
  3. Refine rejects it — the schema expects integer indices ([0, 1, 2, ...]), not string IDs
  4. Agent retries up to 3 times, still produces the wrong format
  5. After 900 seconds of retrying, Refine kills it → goal fails

  This is a systemic agent protocol issue, not a code problem. The code work is done and correct — the agents just can't write a valid signal to hand off. This is likely caused by a Refine version update that changed the expected schema for
  5. After 900 seconds of retrying, Refine kills it → goal fails

  This is a systemic agent protocol issue, not a code problem. The code work is done and correct — the agents just can't write a valid signal to hand off. This is likely caused by a Refine version update that changed the expected schema for
  guidance_applied from string IDs to integer indices, and the agent's prompt hasn't caught up.

  This would explain why so many goals are failing simultaneously — it's not goal-specific, it's the same schema rejection hitting every agent on this node.



[cid:insurity-small2_2f81c33c-d951-4e5c-a467-1113541ca22c.jpg]
Buddy Williams

governance.constitution:
- Refine's components are model (entities), process (supervisor to manage running processes), prompts (LLM templates), surfaces (interfaces into refine), tools (reusable functions for workflow steps), and workflow (defined workflow which calls out to tools). These map directly to src/[model| process|prompts|surfaces|tools|workflow].
- Refine uses a flat file persistence, file-based indexes, in-memory caching, and Rust to maintain high performance. Ensure <50ms performance on CLI and API calls (assuming we are not waiting on LLMs or outside tools).
- Ensure that the architecture is maintained and is consistent. Do not invent new architectural concepts; instead, follow the existing architecture.
- Ensure that documentation, especially src/intent/*, is maintained and the existing document format is preserved.
- Ensure Refine remains "agent-first" by using installed coding-agent CLIs. Do not duplicate coding agent functionality.
